rationale: The closest candidate is P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (set fail-fast: true on the matrix build jobs), but its contraindications apply directly: every matrix outcome is required and full failure diagnostics are required. This workflow builds RPM/deb/AppImage/VM packages for many distros, and each matrix job is a required deliverable consumed by the upload and attach jobs; cancelling remaining builds on the first failure would hide which distros fail and reduce coverage. The synthetic fail-fast experiments are explicitly not recommendations and note that required-check safety needs a separate review. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is not a net new gain because ccache is already restored via actions/cache@v6 in every build job, and distro system-package installation (zypper/dnf/urpmi/apt) is not a safe equivalent dependency cache. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT cannot be safely applied because ci_history contains only failed runs, so there is no representative successful-duration history to derive a timeout that would not break valid slow runs. Scheduled-run patterns (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE) do not fit push/PR/release triggers. No supported optimization preserves the intended build and test coverage while reducing work here.
